findings.claim: The plan assigns agents to edit `project.json`, which violates the path ownership constraint and is ambiguous because two `project.json` files exist.
findings.evidence: Change 1 scope includes "`project.json` command fields" and Change 4 scope includes "`project.json` + `constraints.md` command fields". The constraints say: "`.kbd-orchestrator/` | KBD | Repository-owned state, tracked. Skills other than `/kbd-init` never write `project.json`." The packet also reports `project.json` has "2 matches (.kbd-orchestrator/project.json, .prometheus/project.json)".
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `project.json` edits from implementation changes, or make the exact allowed file and owner action explicit; do not have `/opsx:new` implementation agents modify `.kbd-orchestrator/project.json`.

findings.claim: The Windows evidence scope points to a missing root-level `phases/` path instead of the existing phase directory under `.kbd-orchestrator/`, so evidence will be written to the wrong place.
findings.evidence: Change 6 scope says: "`phases/platform-foundation/evidence/windows.md`". The cited paths section reports "MISSING phases/platform-foundation/evidence/windows.md", while existing phase artifacts are under `.kbd-orchestrator/phases/platform-foundation/` per `assessment.md -> .kbd-orchestrator/phases/platform-foundation/assessment.md`, `analysis.md -> .kbd-orchestrator/phases/platform-foundation/analysis.md`, and `goals.md -> .kbd-orchestrator/phases/platform-foundation/goals.md`.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the scope to `.kbd-orchestrator/phases/platform-foundation/evidence/windows.md`, or explicitly create and justify a new root-level `phases/` convention.

findings.claim: The implementation order contradicts the prior assessment’s required sequencing for Windows-observed behavior.
findings.evidence: The assess handoff says: "CI should land before the EPERM/.cmd defensive code so it can be observed on windows-latest". The plan instead orders `platform-atomic-write-and-lock` and `platform-spawn` in Round 3, with `ci-three-os` only in Round 4.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the minimal CI workflow earlier, before the Windows-specific atomic-write retry and spawn behavior are implemented, or explicitly justify why the assessment sequencing is being rejected and how first-observation evidence will still be preserved.
